code.why: The host process around the fetch: `world-hackernews serve` opens the listener the cli names. The life and the examples walk the pack's fetch on an in-memory World, with no listener (pack-done's serve-check serves it on its own).

Hacker News's API is read-only: no client of the story writes to it, and every read names an item or list the site made; a write, or a read of a location the site never filled, is a client the API does not serve.

A form posted with a token (fnid, hmac) the site did not issue to that signed-in person for that form: the site's own pages always carry their current token, so only a forged or replayed request draws it.
A comment, reply or vote form naming an item that does not exist: the site's pages only link items it holds, so only a crafted request draws it.
A vote whose auth token or direction the site's own arrow did not give: only a forged vote link draws it.
A logout without the signed-in person's logout token: the site's top bar always carries it, so only a cross-site request draws it.
The World's board door (GET /twin/board), which the console reads to lay out Hacker News's pages; it is the twin's own door, which no customer of Hacker News calls.
